items.stem:
The accountant of Mehta and Sons, Pune, finds that the cash book shows a bank balance of ₹86,000 but the bank statement shows ₹1,04,000 on 31 March. The owner Sneha suspects a fraud.
(i) Give two reasons, other than fraud, that could explain the difference. (ii) How will a bank reconciliation statement help Sneha?
items.answer: (i) Cheques issued but not yet presented; interest or direct deposits credited by the bank but not recorded in the cash book. (ii) It lists and explains each cause of difference, shows whether any difference is unexplained (possible error or fraud) and identifies items to enter in the cash book.
items.markingKey: 4 marks: (i) Cheques issued but not yet presented; interest or direct deposits credited by the bank but not recorded in the cash book. (ii) It lists and explains each cause of difference, shows whether any difference is unexplained (possible error or fraud) and identifies items to enter in the cash book.

items.stem:
Nair Stores prepares a bank reconciliation statement only once a year. During the year a clerk deposited fewer cheques than he recorded, and the firm also missed several bank charges.
(i) What would monthly reconciliation have achieved? (ii) Suggest one control along with reconciliation.
items.answer: (i) Errors and the clerk's fraud would have been detected early; bank charges would have been recorded promptly. (ii) Different persons should handle cash and record the cash book (division of duties); counterfoils of pay-in-slips should be checked.
items.markingKey: 4 marks: (i) Errors and the clerk's fraud would have been detected early; bank charges would have been recorded promptly. (ii) Different persons should handle cash and record the cash book (division of duties); counterfoils of pay-in-slips should be checked.

items.stem: Explain any six causes of difference between the cash book and the pass book.
items.answer: (i) Cheques issued but not yet presented for payment: Recorded in the cash book on issue; debited by the bank only when presented. (ii) Cheques deposited but not yet cleared: Recorded in the cash book on deposit; credited by the bank only after clearing. (iii) Bank charges: Debited by the bank; the firm learns of them from the pass book. (iv) Interest allowed by the bank: Credited by the bank directly. (v) Direct deposits by customers: Credited in the pass book before the firm records them. (vi) Direct payments by the bank under standing instructions: Debited in the pass book first. (vii) Dishonour of cheques: Debited by the bank before the firm records it. (viii) Errors in the cash book or the pass book: Mistakes in totalling, posting or recording on either side.
items.markingKey: Any six points, 1 mark each (heading and explanation): (i) Cheques issued but not yet presented for payment: Recorded in the cash book on issue; debited by the bank only when presented. (ii) Cheques deposited but not yet cleared: Recorded in the cash book on deposit; credited by the bank only after clearing. (iii) Bank charges: Debited by the bank; the firm learns of them from the pass book. (iv) Interest allowed by the bank: Credited by the bank directly. (v) Direct deposits by customers: Credited in the pass book before the firm records them. (vi) Direct payments by the bank under standing instructions: Debited in the pass book first. (vii) Dishonour of cheques: Debited by the bank before the firm records it. (viii) Errors in the cash book or the pass book: Mistakes in totalling, posting or recording on either side.
